haiku-low.q1: It does not differ. Both return 401 with "Invalid email or password", run the same statements, and run bcrypt (against a dummy hash when no account exists).
haiku-low.q2: It gets 429 with "Too many failed attempts for this email. Try again in 15 minutes." plus Retry-After. The password is not checked and no failure is recorded.
haiku-low.q3: If the browser sends that cookie, its session is deleted in the same transaction as the new login, whichever user owns it. A fresh session ID is issued.
haiku-low.q4: Only an opaque random session ID, 43 characters. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it. It is also Secure and SameSite=Lax.
haiku-low.q5: It stops working 12 hours after login, even with constant activity. Activity only restarts the 30-minute idle timer, and the 12-hour cap is never extended.
haiku-low.q6: It replies 302 to /login and clears the cookie. Zero matching rows means the session is missing, idle-expired, or past 12 hours.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session row first, then replies. If the delete succeeded or the row was already gone, it redirects to /login and clears the cookie. A database error gives 503 and keeps the cookie.
haiku-low.q8: In the Postgres sessions table, keyed by the SHA-256 hash of the session ID. Both instances share that database, so any instance finds the session by hashing the cookie.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per failed attempt with normalized email and time. The count takes that email's rows with failed_at in the last 10 minutes at each failure.
haiku-low.q10: It runs one UPDATE comparing idle_expires_at with Postgres now(), which also covers the 12-hour cap. On success it writes idle_expires_at = LEAST(now() + 30 min, absolute_expires_at).
haiku-low.q11: 503 login page: "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Try again in a moment." The transaction rolls back, so no new session is created and the old session survives.
haiku-low.q12: A timer in each app process runs every 10 minutes and deletes sessions whose idle_expires_at has passed. Since that never exceeds the 12-hour cap, it also removes absolute-expired sessions.

sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ. Both get the same 401 login page with "Invalid email or password". They run the same statements, including bcrypt (against a dummy hash when no account), so status codes, bodies and timing stay as close as possible.
sonnet.q2: The email is locked (a login_locks row exists, 15 minutes from the 5th failure). The attempt returns a 429 login page ("Too many failed attempts for this email. Try again in 15 minutes.") with a Retry-After header of the remaining lock seconds. The password is not checked and no failure is recorded.
sonnet.q3: On a successful login, a new session ID is always issued. The session named by the incoming cookie, if any (whichever user owns it), is deleted in the same transaction as the new insert. A missing, garbage or unknown cookie deletes nothing. On a 401 or 429 the old session is left untouched.
sonnet.q4: Only the opaque random session ID (32 random bytes, 43 base64url characters). Page scripts cannot read it because it is HttpOnly.
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after login (the absolute expiry). Activity restarts the 30-minute idle timer but never extends the 12-hour cap, so the session stops working then.
sonnet.q6: The UPDATE touch-and-check returns zero rows. The server replies 302 to /login and clears the cookie (Max-Age=0). The sweep later removes any leftover row.
sonnet.q7: With a cookie, the server hashes it and deletes the matching session row before any reply. If the delete succeeds or the row was already gone, it replies 302 to /login and clears the cookie. If there is no cookie, the result is the same 302 and clearing. (If the database errors, it returns 503 and keeps the cookie.)
sonnet.q8: In the Postgres sessions table, which is shared by both instances. Any instance hashes the cookie's session ID with SHA-256 and runs the UPDATE on sessions WHERE id_hash matches. No sticky sessions are needed.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table, one row per failed attempt (email, failed_at). At each failure the server counts that email's rows with failed_at in the 10 minutes before now (a sliding window, using Postgres now()).
sonnet.q10: It compares idle_expires_at with Postgres now() in the WHERE clause of the single UPDATE (id_hash = hash of the cookie AND idle_expires_at > now()). When it matches, it writes back idle_expires_at = LEAST(now() + 30 minutes, absolute_expires_at) and returns user_id.
sonnet.q11: A 503 login page: "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Try again in a moment." The transaction rolls back, so no session is created, no cookie is set, and the old session is not deleted.
sonnet.q12: The cleanup sweep. Each app instance runs it every 10 minutes and deletes in batches of about 1000 rows. It deletes sessions where idle_expires_at <= now(), which also covers sessions past their absolute expiry.
